core_statement: For any finite positive environment measure and any bounded measurable kernel, the supremum over cap-one product marginals equals the supremum over products of indicators of arbitrary measure-one sets; the extreme sets can be selected once after averaging over the whole environment. Applied to quadratic interval kernels, arbitrary conditioning-generated affine fields and outside positive localization are zero-tax. The newest partner BV obstruction plus diagonal normalization shows Gaussian regularize-and-renormalize loses at least N^2 in Hessian scale on N-fragment reflection examples.

fixed_source.result_applied: Theorem A: three-dimensional all-eigenvalues-at-least-sigma affine quadratic density bound 6 sqrt(pi)/sigma
fixed_source.application: For B_*=I-(2/3)11^T and arbitrary outside C,D, conditioning outside variables gives ||p_Q||_infty <= 6 sqrt(pi).

partner_applied.use: N-fragment extreme laws require inverse-half-scale moment at least N sqrt(2pi); after diagonal normalization the reflection Hessian operator norm is at most (N-o(1))^-2.

remaining_gap: After exact reduction to arbitrary measurable unit-measure sets, a full proof still needs a matrix-geometric whole-law receiver that works directly on those rough sets before any BV, fragment-count, diameter, Gaussian-scale or moment parameter is paid.
